**Continuous 2.38.12**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.38.11, 2.38.10, 2.38.9, 2.38.8, 2.38.7, 2.38.6, 2.38.5, 2.38.4, 2.38.3, 2.38.2, 2.38.1, 2.38.0, 2.36.0, 2.34.0, 2.32.0, 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.38.12.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.38.12.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.38.12.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.38.12.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.38.12.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.38.12.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.38.12.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.38.12-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.38.12.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.38.12-vscode/continuous-cli-2.38.12.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.38.11

A fix for a crash in 2.38.11. If your chat panel went blank with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'chip')`, update to this version; your settings are kept.

### Fixes

- **The chat panel no longer crashes on a level saved by an older version.** 2.38.11 removed the IDGAF level, but the panel keeps its last levels between sessions, so anyone whose saved levels still said `idgaf` or `yolo` got a blank panel. A saved level is now read as Permissive (Delegate on Questions), and a value this version does not know becomes that area's default. The level chips also fall back to the Cautious look instead of failing on an unknown level.
- **`tools=delegate` is no longer accepted for Tool use.** Delegate is a Questions level only; a level set on any other area is read as that area's default, wherever it comes from.
